- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward to capture mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overreacts with exaggerated continuation; dampen forecast slope for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- Model tends to lag in early periods of strong sentiment shifts; add 1–2 days of lead time adjustment for sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows persistent divergence from 18-day history, reduce forecast volatility by 10–15% to reflect diminishing momentum.
